t: You're on Queen Victoria Street, which runs through the City of London from Victoria Embankment and New Bridge Street, heading east to the Bank junction. Beyond Bank, the road carries on as Threadneedle Street. Along the way it meets Cannon Street, Walbrook and Poultry. The street is named in honour of Queen Victoria, who reigned from 1837 to 1901, longer than any monarch before her. Her sixty-three years gave us the Victorian era, a time of industrial, political, scientific and military change, and a great expansion of the British Empire.
